key_insight: The paper introduces FCV-PICRN, a physics-informed convolutional residual network with Fourier features and complex-valued learning that can reconstruct missing, sparse, and noisy flow fields even in dynamically critical regions.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to recover velocity, pressure, and vorticity from incomplete experimental or simulation data in wakes and turbulence where conventional interpolation and standard PINNs struggle.
method: Fourier-feature embedding captures oscillatory, multiscale flow structures.
Complex-valued representations learn coupled amplitude-phase flow dynamics.
Navier--Stokes-constrained convolutional residual blocks enforce physical consistency during reconstruction.
evidence_signal: Validated on Taylor--Green vortex and cylinder wake at Re=100, then tested on severely gappy noisy wake cases and 2D Kolmogorov turbulence, with strong SSIM/PSNR and lower error than a conventional PINN.
watch_item: Performance still depends on the quality of physics constraints and training setup, so extreme noise, different Reynolds numbers, or poorly tuned gap geometries may reduce reconstruction reliability.
paper_title: Fourier-Feature-Embedded Complex-Valued Physics-Informed Convolutional Residual Networks for Sparse and Gappy Noisy Flow-Field Reconstruction
